observed_title: Moderate Deviations of Hitting Times for Trajectories of Sums of Independent and Identically Distributed Random Variables
version: arXiv:2311.05409v1, 9 November 2023 visible watermark; nine PDF pages; external metadata not reverified

read_ranges.scope: Full article: assumptions, main theorem, cited path MDP/LDP, all proofs, simulations and references; important pages1,2,4,6,8,9 visually checked

proof_verification: local_source_errors_checked_and_repairs_separated; external Hu–Lee/Schuette path theorems not independently certified

topic_relevance.H01: direct for logarithmic moderate deviation of iid path hitting time; not a Cramér normal relative-tail ratio
topic_relevance.H04: adjacent path rate minimization and unique-zero argument; not finite-threshold exact tail

definitions.name: Interpolated iid path
definitions.statement: S̃_n(t)=Σ_{i≤floor(nt)}X_i+(nt−floor(nt))X_floor(nt)+1; μ=EX1>0, σ²=VarX1. Deterministic x(t)=μt and τr=r/μ for fixed 0<r<μ. Source first defines t∈[0,1], later uses arbitrary T; define/extend the iid path for all t≥0 or explicitly isolate no-hit event.

definitions.name: Assumptions1.1–1.2
definitions.statement: Λ(a)=logEe^(aX1) finite and continuous for every real a, sup_a[−Λ(a)]<∞; some θ∈(0,1], v>1,b>0 satisfy Eexp(θ|X1|^v)≤e^b. Main quotient additionally needs σ²>0; variance zero is not a valid literal denominator.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem1.4
assumptions: The preceding iid hypotheses and nonzero variance; fixed r∈(0,μ), fixed t>0; positive a_n with a_n/n→0 and sqrt(n)/a_n→0.
theorem_cards.statement: For both strict events (n/a_n)(τr^n−τr)>t and <−t, lim (n/a_n²)logP=−μ³t²/(2σ²r). Speed is a_n²/n; this supplies only logarithmic asymptotics, not ratio to 1−Φ or saddlepoint prefactor.
proof_steps: Hu–Lee cited path MDP uses I_T(f)=∫₀ᵀ(f′)²/(2σ²) for f absolutely continuous,f(0)=0. Endpoint energy inf_{f(T)=a}I_T=a²/(2σ²T) follows by Cauchy–Schwarz, attained f(t)=at/T.
Schuette cited path LDP upper bound with J_T=∫Λ*(f′) plus goodness/unique zero yields P(|τr^n−τr|>δ)≤exp(−cδ n) asymptotically. Since n²/a_n²→∞, this error is superexponential at MDP speed.

On finite hit and |τr^n−τr|≤δ, S̃_n(τr^n)=nr converts late hitting into θ_n(τr^n)<−μt. Closed inf-window set Fδ gives upper bound; open sup-window set Gδ and linear negative test path give lower bound. First n→∞ then δ,ε→0.
For the upper inf-window energy, write uniform I≥μ²t²/[2σ²(τr+δ)] rather than retaining a witness s(δ) depending on f after an infimum. Same limit follows.
gaps: The source proves (1.2) in detail and says (1.3) analogously, without full printed proof. Use source assertion for the early branch unless supplied separately.

The original [0,1] hitting definition allows τ=∞ if no hit; equation(3.3) is not literal on that event. Extend path or discard no-hit event with exp(−cn) bound, choose δ<min(τr,1−τr); this local repair does not certify cited path results.
Source references Hu–Lee as 2001 but prints Transactions AMS355(8) citation; exact bibliographic identity/date not independently checked.

theorem_cards.label: Rate-function zero and attainment error
theorem_cards.statement: Λ*(x)=sup_a(ax−Λ(a))≥0 and equals0 iff x=μ for finite differentiable Λ around0 and σ²>0. Source claims concavity implies one and only one attained maximum for every slope; this is false at support endpoints.
proof_steps: For x≠μ, derivative of ax−Λ(a) at0 is x−μ; choose a small signed parameter to get a strictly positive value. For x=μ, Jensen gives Λ(a)≥aμ, so supremum=0. Thus J_T=0 forces f′=μ a.e., hence f(t)=μt.
Counterexample satisfying the written assumptions: X=0 or2 with equal probabilities. For x=0, Λ*(0)=log2 but supremum reached only as a→−∞; no finite maximizer.
gaps: Goodness of J_T comes from cited theorem; unique-zero local argument does not prove whole path LDP.

theorem_cards.label: Section4 examples and graph sign
theorem_cards.statement: a_n=n^0.9 is a valid MDP scale, but Example1 Exp(1) violates all-real mgf, bounded sup[−Λ], and superexponential-power moment assumptions; Example2 Poisson(1) has all-real mgf and bounded sup[−Λ]=1 but Eexp(θX^v)=∞ for every θ>0,v>1. Neither example follows by direct invocation of Theorem1.4 as printed.
proof_steps: Exp mgf=1/(1−a) only a<1; −Λ(a)=log(1−a)→∞ as a→−∞; θx^v−x→∞ so powered exponential moment diverges.
Poisson k-th summand exp(θk^v−1−log(k!)) does not tend to zero since k^v dominates k logk. This is a necessary failure of Assumption1.2.

PDF p8 and p9 graph axes and legends display nonpositive scaled log probability and red −2t². The displayed simulation formula contains a leading minus before log, which would be nonnegative. Treat the formula sign as a source inconsistency; no Monte Carlo code is supplied to decide actual implementation.
gaps: Experiments at n=100 and 10000 replicates do not certify limit, uniformity, or theorem applicability. Exponential/Poisson hitting MDP may hold under another theorem but it is not established here by the printed hypotheses.
